newsitem.title: UK: Shell Q2 earnings hit by pound.
newsitem.headline: Shell Q2 earnings hit by pound.

text.p: Oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell Group on Thursday reported a four percent fall in second-quarter profits, hit by the strength of the pound which masked an underlying three percent rise over last year.

Net earnings excluding special items were 1.14 billion pounds ($1.8 billion) in the quarter, making 2.69 for the half year. Shell said higher production largely offset lower crude oil prices, while chemical earnings were slightly down in the quarter.
Shell shares fell in London and Amsterdam after the results, which came in below market forecasts which ranged between 1.26 and 1.48 billion pounds.
Shell said refining and marketing margins were up 17 percent in the quarter on a current cost basis, but reported earnings were lower because of inventory holding losses.
Corporate items in the period included currency exchange losses of 117 million pounds due largely to the strength of sterling over the quarter.
Crude oil prices in the first half were about $1.5 below a year earlier due to resumption of exports from Iraq and increased non-OPEC production.

The company said the outlook was for continued increases in crude oil supply from the North Sea and ample supply of oil products. But the price background should provide an improved basis for chemicals industry performance for the remainder of the year, it said.
The group spent 1.7 billion pounds on capital investment and exploration in the quarter and said spending was set to step up in the second half, mainly on exploration and production.

Shell shares, which have had a strong run recently, were down 30 pence to 443 after the results, while in Amsterdam, shares in the Dutch arm, Royal Dutch, fell 4.70 guilders to 115.50. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
